clue.text: Rose made to look good?

definitions.meaning: rose as the past tense of rise, meaning stood or got out of bed
dressed and groomed elaborately, decked out in finery

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: to have risen from bed, and to have been dressed up smartly.

clue.text: The man about to call may be threatening

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man
c, short for circa, means about
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A man about to make a phone call might be making threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectoring is bullying and intimidating talk, a synonym of threatening in its adjectival sense.

clue.text: 'Wormy' fellow following female priest

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the fellow is placed behind the female priest

parts.note: Ann is a female name
Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel
Dan is a man's name, so stands for any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone with a worm-like character trails behind a woman priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' could be DON or DEN as easily as DAN; only DAN gives the worm word.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelidan means relating to the annelids, the ringed worms such as earthworms, hence wormy.

clue.text: Trickster from political party meeting Queen

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A con artist emerges from a party that has just met the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A duper is one who dupes, that is cheats or deceives, so a trickster.

clue.text: Sweet son abandoning wilderness

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so one letter is dropped from the pudding

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding or dessert

explanation.surface: A son leaves the pudding course and heads off into the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' takes one S from DESSERT, leaving the arid landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is barren, uninhabited land, a wilderness.

clue.text: Enlighten a bishop when there's lack of employment about

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for idleness wraps round the other letters

parts.note: disuse is a state of not being employed or used
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop tries to enlighten people in a time of unemployment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts AB inside DISUSE; 'employment' means use, not jobs, despite the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To disabuse someone is to free them from a mistaken belief, so to enlighten them.

clue.text: Spooner's forever laughing maybe in Scottish water

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famous for swapping word beginnings, signals the initial letters are exchanged

parts.note: for aye, written as one word, means for ever
laughing is one example of mirth

explanation.surface: Someone forever laughing in a Scottish stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: FORAY MIRTH with F and M swapped. The Moray Firth is a large inlet on the northeast coast of Scotland, near Inverness.
explanation.definitionFit: A firth is a Scottish sea inlet, and this one is named after the old county of Moray.

clue.text: Sign of sorrow that comes with RIP

definitions.meaning: a drop from the eye shed in grief
a rip is a split or rent in fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals of RIP suggest the gravestone 'rest in peace', fitting the sorrow; ignore them and a rip is a split. The two senses are pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of grief and a rent in cloth share this spelling, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Sleep with one end of eiderdown touching this?

definitions.text: Sleep with one end of eiderdown touching this?

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: one end of a word here is its opening letter, taken from the bedding word

explanation.surface: Asleep in bed, with the quilt's edge brushing the back of your neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the edge of the eiderdown touches the back of a sleeper's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the neck is where a pulled-up eiderdown's edge rests on a sleeper.

clue.text: Criticises cuts when one misses out

indicators.note: misses out means omits, so one letter is left out of the longer word

parts.note: depreciates means reduces or cuts in value
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone criticises spending cuts when a person loses out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses out' removes I from DEPRECIATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to express disapproval of, so it is a synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Advocate favouring car in broadcast

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A supporter favours a car appearing in a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In broadcast' says MOTOR is heard, giving MOTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter is one who advocates or champions a cause or a person.

clue.text: Something brought up by Sloaney girl in club

parts.note: cud is the food a cow regurgitates to chew again
gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl, as said by a Sloane Ranger, a posh young Londoner

explanation.surface: A posh girl at a nightclub brings something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon, a club.

clue.text: Returning without excitement, I collected message

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
collected means gathered in, so the dull word takes the single letter into itself

parts.note: lame means dull and uninspiring

explanation.surface: Coming home from an unexciting time, I picked up a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' puts I in LAME to make LIAME; 'Returning' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic letter sent over the internet is a message.

clue.text: Detail put out that says nothing new

indicators.note: out means put wrong or disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detail is discarded because it adds nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is fodder, not part of the indicator: DETAILPUT, nine letters, rearranged by 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a comment repeated so often it offers nothing fresh.

clue.text: Protected army officer before in building away from house?

indicators.note: in places the officer and the old word for before inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding set apart from the house
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An officer took cover in an outbuilding in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building away from house' is a cryptic way to say outbuilding; ERE is old-fashioned for before.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means protected from harm or the weather, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Aim to get to street meeting with another person

parts.note: to try is to attempt or aim to do

explanation.surface: Someone aims to reach a street where they have a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting arranged between lovers.

clue.text: One may get involved in dramas with gun?

definitions.text: One may get involved in dramas with gun?

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: Who might get caught up in theatrical scenes with a firearm?
explanation.walkthrough: DRAMAS and GUN together are the nine letters; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of a guards regiment, armed with a rifle, could be caught up in dramatic events.

clue.text: Sharp sounds from objects hard to ignore

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so a letter is dropped from the word for objects

parts.note: things are objects
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Sharp noises from items so hard they cannot be overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To ignore' drops H from THINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ting is a high clear ringing sound like a struck glass, a sharp sound.

clue.text: Friends round Norse goddess sacrificing ace horses

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for friends goes either side

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, so one letter is surrendered by the goddess

parts.note: Freya is the Norse goddess of love
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Friends surround a Norse goddess who sacrifices horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacrificing' leaves FREY once the ace goes. Freya (also Freyja) is the Norse goddess of love; palfreys were medieval riding horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A palfrey is a gentle riding horse of the Middle Ages, so these are horses.

clue.text: Keep quiet about outlandish idea's content

indicators.note: content as in what something contains, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: Say nothing about the substance of a bizarre notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' (stressed on the first syllable) gives the letters inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to conceal it, to keep quiet about it.

clue.text: Court needs prisoner's background in the East End

parts.note: a con is a prisoner, short for convict

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop the initial h, so it goes

parts.note: a person's history is their background

explanation.surface: A court requires a convict's history, as told in Cockney London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the East End' drops the H from HISTORY, as the Cockney accent of East London does.
explanation.definitionFit: A consistory is a church court, such as the papal senate or a bishop's diocesan court.

clue.text: Arab location as home for Lord and Master?

indicators.note: home for means housing, so the country contains the abbreviation

parts.note: Oman is a country of Arabia

explanation.surface: An Arabian place serves as the residence of a lord and master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord and Master' is a jokey phrase for a husband; the question mark flags the informal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the boss or the husband, the master of the house, is called this.

clue.text: Naughty kid with naughty books 'making the wrong choices'?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
rude can mean naughty or risque
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A mischievous child with smutty magazines is clearly choosing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or rash, describing someone making poor decisions.

clue.text: Pig in ravine

definitions.meaning: to pig is to eat greedily
a narrow valley between steep rocky walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' looks like a noun for an animal, but it is a verb, eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is to stuff oneself, and a deep narrow rocky valley shares the word.

clue.text: Servant I'm employing is such a punctual one?

definitions.text: Servant I'm employing is such a punctual one?

parts.words: Servant I'm employing is such a punctual one?
parts.note: the phrase servanT IM Employing holds a four-letter word for a period, so the phrase guards it, and a punctual person also does so

explanation.walkthrough: The words 'Servant I'm employing' hold TIME in their letters, so they are its keeper; the answer is also a punctual servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who records hours, or is reliably on schedule, is described this way.

clue.text: Agent given sack had to be rogue

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
to sack is to plunder, to rob
had as in ate, eating a meal

explanation.surface: An agent who has been fired must have been a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal, but it is plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, a rogue.

clue.text: Tough Listener puzzles absorbing one

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the rearranged letters swallow the numeral
puzzles as a verb means confuses, so the letters of the magazine word are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Listener crossword is hard, absorbing one completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously difficult crossword series. 'Puzzles' rearranges its letters into RESLIENT, and 'absorbing' takes the numeral in.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means able to withstand hardship, tough.

clue.text: Get to come to know a Conservative, pleasingly old-world

parts.note: quaint means attractively old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Getting to know a charmingly old-fashioned Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone is to make them familiar with something, causing them to come to know it.

clue.text: Room available from landlord I must occupy

indicators.note: occupy means fill or take up residence in, so the letter goes inside the phrase

parts.note: to let is what a landlord's sign says of a property for rent

explanation.surface: A room the landlord has free, which I must move into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must occupy' puts I into TO LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilet is a lavatory, the room containing a WC.

clue.text: Crowd that may gather when news is expected

definitions.meaning: to crowd someone is to push in on them

definitions.text: that may gather when news is expected
definitions.meaning: journalists collectively, who assemble outside places awaiting a story

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the verb, push close; the second is the reporters who gather outside, say, a hospital awaiting an announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd is to push, and journalists as a body are also called by this word.

clue.text: University dean's first to join in cheery college party

indicators.note: join in means enter, so the letters go inside the word for cheery

parts.note: gay in its older sense means cheerful

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word for the senior academic

explanation.surface: A university dean is first to join in a cheerful college party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To join in' puts U and D inside GAY. A gaudy is an annual college feast at Oxford, mostly for old members.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaudy is a celebratory dinner or reunion held by a college, especially at Oxford.

clue.text: Senior Catholic dignitary not half showing heart?

indicators.note: not half means losing half, so the second four letters of the title go

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior official of the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A cardinal, only half there, shows his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' cuts CARDINAL to its first four letters. 'Heart' tempts towards medicine, but the question mark shows it is an example: a heart is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart is one of the four suits, so a heart is an example of a playing card.
